challenge.better_approach: Reading SSH_CONNECTION from the environment was looked at: CC's own shells can unset it and a local shell can set it, so the environment cannot be the gate (caller() already rules the environment may never upgrade a class). The process tree is kernel truth. Classing session-*.scope under sshd as unknown was rejected: it would change every journal entry's class, which is 62e7bff757c0's job once keys exist.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That no local path to approve descends from sshd. The listener (pid 1729, comm sshd) is parent only of ssh logins. And that Akien approves at the box, which the guard forces until 62e7bff757c0 lands.
challenge.prior_art: caller() already walks ancestry() for a cc ancestor (ticket 8a53046951bb); this adds one more ancestor test on the same walk.
challenge.real_collision: none: outline 17.2.2 asks for exactly this; 62e7bff757c0 later tells CC from Akien by key and may lift the guard for Akien's key.

answers.falsifier: Done when an akien-scope caller under sshd-session is refused by approve and the same caller at the box is not; wrong intent if an ssh login's shell does not descend from sshd-session (measured: it does, pid 1520928 under 1520885, session-4397.scope).
answers.from_idea: none, because it is the interim guard outline 17.2.2 names (cairn/devices/cairn/requirements/17-tools.md, -amm), answered at Q#115 (CairnCommons/questions/open-0bfaf0f5aa8b.json)
answers.how: ancestry() records each pid's /proc/<pid>/comm; caller() carries ssh = the pid of the first ancestor named sshd-session (or sshd, the older OpenSSH child), only when one is found; approve() refuses a caller carrying ssh before its class check. A red-first proof injects the ancestry as test_the_caller_reads_whose_terminal_it_is.py does.
answers.traces_to: Law 6: the owner alone gates writes, and approve is Akien's gate; a CC over ssh classed akien is an ambient pass through it. Outline 17.2.2 (-amm).
answers.what: The artifact door's approve refuses any caller that descends from an ssh login, Akien's included, until CC has its own ssh key.

bullets.text: Measured 2026-11-18: an ssh login's shell sits in session-4397.scope, which classify() reads as akien, under sshd-session (OpenSSH 10.2p1).
Guard (a) splits per Q#103: this ticket is the artifact door's approve; the trouble device's operator close is a second ticket.
